lessons.title: Lesson 1: Hello World & Main Method
lessons.html:
Your First Java Program

Java is a class-based, object-oriented language especially designed for web development.

Basic Structure:

  • public class - Main class declaration
  • public static void main - Entry point where program starts
  • System.out.println - Prints text to console
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, Java!");
    }
}

Compile: javac HelloWorld.java
Run: java HelloWorld
Practice: Change message to your name!

Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding the fundamental concepts is crucial for advanced topics
  • Always consider edge cases and error handling in production code
  • Practice with real-world examples to solidify your knowledge

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Variables & Data Types
lessons.html:
Variables and Data Types

All variables must be declared with their type before use. Java is statically typed.

Primitive Types:

TypeSizeExample
int4 bytes42
double8 bytes3.14
boolean1 bittrue
char2 bytes'A'
public class Variables {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int age = 25;
        double salary = 50000.50;
        String name = "Alice";
        boolean isActive = true;
        System.out.println(name + " is " + age + " years old");
    }
}

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Control Structures
lessons.html:
Control Flow Statements

Control structures change the order of execution based on conditions.

if/else:

int age = 20;
if (age >= 18) {
    System.out.println("Adult");
} else {
    System.out.println("Minor");
}

switch:

int day = 1;
switch(day) {
    case 1: System.out.println("Monday"); break;
    case 2: System.out.println("Tuesday"); break;
    default: System.out.println("Other day");
}

Loops:

for(int i=0; i<5; i++) {
    System.out.print(i + " ");
}
// Output: 0 1 2 3 4

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Methods & Arrays
lessons.html:
Methods and Arrays

Methods are reusable blocks of code. Arrays store multiple values of same type.

Method Example:

public static int add(int a, int b) {
    return a + b;
}

Arrays:

public class ArraysExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int[] numbers = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
        for(int num : numbers) {
            System.out.println(num);
        }
        System.out.println("Length: " + numbers.length);
    }
}

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Object-Oriented Basics
lessons.html:
Classes and Objects

Java is object-oriented. Everything revolves around classes and objects.

Class Definition:

class Person {
    String name;
    int age;
    
    void introduce() {
        System.out.println("Hi, I'm " + name);
    }
}

Creating Objects:

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Person p = new Person();
        p.name = "Bob";
        p.age = 30;
        p.introduce();  // Hi, I'm Bob
    }
}

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Constructors & this Keyword
lessons.html:
Constructors and the this Reference

Constructors initialize new objects. The 'this' keyword refers to the current object instance.

Constructors:

class Student {
    String name;
    int age;
    String studentId;

    // Default constructor
    public Student() {
        this.name = "Unknown";
        this.age = 18;
    }

    // Parameterized constructor
    public Student(String name, int age) {
        this.name = name;
        this.age = age;
    }

    // Constructor chaining
    public Student(String name, int age, String studentId) {
        this(name, age);  // Calls the 2-param constructor
        this.studentId = studentId;
    }

    // Copy constructor
    public Student(Student other) {
        this(other.name, other.age, other.studentId);
    }

    void display() {
        System.out.println(name + " (ID: " + studentId + ")");
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a BankAccount class with account number, balance, and owner
  2. Add multiple constructors including a copy constructor
  3. Implement a method that returns the current object using this

Key Takeaways:

  • Constructors have the same name as the class
  • this() calls another constructor in the same class
  • Copy constructors create a new object from an existing one

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Inheritance Basics
lessons.html:
Extending Classes

Inheritance creates is-a relationships between classes. Subclasses inherit fields and methods from parents.

Basic Inheritance:

// Parent class
class Animal {
    String name;

    public Animal(String name) {
        this.name = name;
    }

    public void eat() {
        System.out.println(name + " is eating");
    }

    public void sleep() {
        System.out.println(name + " is sleeping");
    }
}

// Child class
class Dog extends Animal {
    String breed;

    public Dog(String name, String breed) {
        super(name);  // Call parent constructor
        this.breed = breed;
    }

    public void bark() {
        System.out.println(name + " barks!");
    }

    @Override
    public void eat() {
        super.eat();  // Call parent method
        System.out.println(name + " wags tail while eating");
    }
}

Using the Classes:

Dog dog = new Dog("Buddy", "Golden Retriever");
dog.eat();   // Buddy is eating + Buddy wags tail while eating
dog.sleep(); // Buddy is sleeping (inherited)
dog.bark();  // Buddy barks! (added behavior)

// Polymorphism
Animal pet = new Dog("Max", "Beagle");
pet.eat();  // Calls Dog's eat method
// pet.bark();  // Error! Animal doesn't have bark()

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a Shape hierarchy with Circle, Rectangle, Triangle
  2. Add a calculateArea() method overridden in each subclass
  3. Use polymorphism with an array of Shape references

Key Takeaways:

  • extends keyword creates inheritance
  • super calls parent constructor or methods
  • @Override redefines a parent method

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Polymorphism & Abstract Classes
lessons.html:
Abstract Classes and Dynamic Binding

Abstract classes define common behavior that subclasses must implement. Polymorphism enables flexible code.

Abstract Class:

abstract class Shape {
    protected String color;

    public Shape(String color) {
        this.color = color;
    }

    public String getColor() { return color; }

    // Abstract method - subclasses MUST implement
    public abstract double getArea();

    // Concrete method - shared behavior
    public void display() {
        System.out.println(color + " shape with area: " + getArea());
    }
}

class Circle extends Shape {
    private double radius;

    public Circle(String color, double radius) {
        super(color);
        this.radius = radius;
    }

    @Override
    public double getArea() {
        return Math.PI * radius * radius;
    }
}

class Rectangle extends Shape {
    private double width, height;

    public Rectangle(String color, double width, double height) {
        super(color);
        this.width = width;
        this.height = height;
    }

    @Override
    public double getArea() {
        return width * height;
    }
}

Polymorphic Usage:

Shape[] shapes = {
    new Circle("Red", 5),
    new Rectangle("Blue", 4, 6),
    new Circle("Green", 3)
};

for (Shape shape : shapes) {
    shape.display();  // Correct area method called dynamically
    System.out.println("Area: " + shape.getArea());
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create an abstract Vehicle class with subclasses Car and Bike
  2. Add an abstract method startEngine() with different implementations
  3. Write a method that accepts any Shape and prints its area

Key Takeaways:

  • Abstract classes cannot be instantiated directly
  • Abstract methods must be implemented by subclasses
  • Polymorphism calls the correct method at runtime

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Interfaces & Multiple Inheritance
lessons.html:
Interfaces and Contracts

Interfaces define contracts that classes can implement. Java supports multiple inheritance only through interfaces.

Interface Definition:

interface Drawable {
    void draw();

    // Default method (Java 8+)
    default void printInfo() {
        System.out.println("Drawable object");
    }

    // Static method
    static Drawable createCircle() {
        return () -> System.out.println("Drawing circle");
    }
}

interface Resizable {
    void resize(double factor);
}

// Multiple interface implementation
class GraphicShape implements Drawable, Resizable {
    private String name;

    public GraphicShape(String name) {
        this.name = name;
    }

    @Override
    public void draw() {
        System.out.println("Drawing " + name);
    }

    @Override
    public void resize(double factor) {
        System.out.println("Resizing " + name + " by " + factor);
    }
}

Functional Interface (Lambda Ready):

@FunctionalInterface
interface Calculator {
    int calculate(int a, int b);

    // Only ONE abstract method allowed
}

// Lambda usage
Calculator add = (a, b) -> a + b;
Calculator multiply = (a, b) -> a * b;

System.out.println(add.calculate(5, 3));       // 8
System.out.println(multiply.calculate(5, 3));  // 15

Practice Exercises:

  1. Define interfaces for a plugin system
  2. Create functional interfaces and use them with lambdas
  3. Implement Comparable interface for custom sorting

Key Takeaways:

  • Interfaces define contracts without implementation
  • A class can implement multiple interfaces
  • Functional interfaces enable lambda expressions

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Exception Handling
lessons.html:
Handling Errors Gracefully

Java exceptions handle runtime errors. Checked exceptions must be declared or caught.

Try-Catch-Finally:

import java.io.*;

public class FileProcessor {
    public String readFirstLine(String filename) {
        BufferedReader reader = null;
        try {
            reader = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(filename));
            return reader.readLine();
        } catch (FileNotFoundException e) {
            System.err.println("File not found: " + filename);
            return null;
        } catch (IOException e) {
            System.err.println("Error reading file: " + e.getMessage());
            return null;
        } finally {
            // Always executes
            try {
                if (reader != null) reader.close();
            } catch (IOException e) {
                System.err.println("Error closing reader");
            }
        }
    }

    // Try-with-resources (Java 7+)
    public String readFirstLineModern(String filename) {
        try (BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(filename))) {
            return reader.readLine();
        } catch (IOException e) {
            System.err.println("Error: " + e.getMessage());
            return null;
        }
    }
}

Custom Exception:

class InsufficientFundsException extends Exception {
    private double balance;
    private double amount;

    public InsufficientFundsException(double balance, double amount) {
        super(String.format("Insufficient funds: balance=%.2f, requested=%.2f", balance, amount));
        this.balance = balance;
        this.amount = amount;
    }

    public double getBalance() { return balance; }
    public double getShortfall() { return amount - balance; }
}

class BankAccount {
    private double balance;

    public void withdraw(double amount) throws InsufficientFundsException {
        if (amount > balance) {
            throw new InsufficientFundsException(balance, amount);
        }
        balance -= amount;
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a custom validation exception
  2. Implement a retry mechanism for network operations
  3. Write a method that throws multiple checked exceptions

Key Takeaways:

  • Checked exceptions must be caught or declared with throws
  • Try-with-resources auto-closes Closeable resources
  • Custom exceptions provide domain-specific error info
